args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-half-even-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring.

Change: switch `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

CI: run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug on a new branch. CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer.

- **The bug:** `src/money.py` was rounding with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, even though its own comment says it uses banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) per FIN-212. That's why the nightly test failed: 2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of the expected 2.66.
- **The fix:** I changed `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. It's a one-line change, committed to branch `fix/money-half-even-rounding`.
- **CI:** run ci-0001 passed.
- **PR:** #101 (https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101). I haven't merged it, because merging into main needs a code owner's approval.

The advisory tool doesn't recognise FIN-212, so I couldn't check the requirement against its source. The fix matches what the test and the code comment both say.

This changes how every amount that ends in exactly half a cent gets rounded: when the cent digit is even, it now rounds down instead of up. Before merging, check whether anything else that uses `round_money` depends on the old behaviour.
